records.source: Τολμᾷ τις ὑμῶν πρᾶγμα ἔχων πρὸς τὸν ἕτερον κρίνεσθαι ἐπὶ τῶν ἀδίκων, καὶ οὐχὶ ἐπὶ τῶν ἁγίων;
records.gloss: Dares anyone of you a matter having against the other to be judged before the unrighteous, and not before the holy [ones]?
pieces: When one of you has a dispute with another, how can you dare to take it to court before the unrighteous instead of before God's holy people?

L.1: Does any of you, having a matter against another, dare to go to law before the unrighteous, and not before the holy ones?

R.1: Suppose one of you has a complaint against another believer. How can you dare to take it to a court where unbelievers are the judges? Why not bring it to God's people instead?

decisions.choice: a lawsuit over a civil matter, brought before the city's courts
decisions.reason: πρᾶγμα was used of a legal case, and κρίνεσθαι of going to law or having one's case decided. Corinth was a Roman colony, and civil cases were heard before its magistrates. Verses 4 and 7-8 show that the cases were about property and money, matters of everyday life.

decisions.choice: the unrighteous: people outside God's people, here the judges of the city's courts
alternatives: judges who were corrupt or took bribes
decisions.reason: ἀδίκων is set against ἁγίων; ("the holy ones"), and verse 6 calls the same people ἀπίστων; ("unbelievers"). Paul describes their standing before God, not their honesty as judges. The word prepares for verse 9, where the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God, and verse 8, where the believers themselves do wrong.

decisions.choice: the holy ones: the believers, the people God has set apart as his own
alternatives: especially holy members of the church
decisions.reason: As in 1:2, the holy ones are the whole church, called to belong to God. Paul is asking why the church does not settle the matter within itself.

decisions.choice: dare: an indignant question, asking how anyone can bring himself to do this
decisions.reason: Τολμᾷ stands first for emphasis. Paul is not asking for information; he is shocked that a believer would do such a thing.

decisions.choice: go to law (L); take it to court (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb means having one's case decided by a court; English says this with "go to law" or "take to court".

decisions.choice: holy ones (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: As in Philippians and Colossians: "saints" now suggests especially good people, but Paul means every believer.

decisions.choice: another believer; a court where unbelievers are the judges
decisions.reason: Readable says who the parties and the judges are (m2), and splits the question in two.

records.heading: Lawsuits between believers

records.source: ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ ἅγιοι τὸν κόσμον κρινοῦσιν;
records.gloss: Or not do you know that the holy [ones] the world will judge?
pieces: Or do you not know that God's holy people will judge the world?

L.2: Or do you not know that the holy ones will judge the world?

R.2: Do you not know that God's people will judge the world?

decisions.choice: do you not know: a rebuke; they should know this
decisions.reason: Paul uses this question six times in this chapter (verses 2, 3, 9, 15, 16, 19), as in 3:16, each time reminding them of something they already know but are not living by.

decisions.choice: God's people will share in judging the world at the end
alternatives: their way of life will show up the world's wrong by contrast
decisions.reason: Scripture speaks of the holy ones receiving judgment and the kingdom (Daniel 7:22, 27), of the twelve judging the tribes of Israel (Matthew 19:28), and of thrones of judgment given to the faithful (Revelation 20:4). Paul assumes the Corinthians know this teaching.

decisions.choice: the world: humankind apart from God, which will face his judgment
decisions.reason: κόσμον here means people, the world that God judges (11:32; Romans 3:6).

decisions.choice: holy ones (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

records.source: καὶ εἰ ἐν ὑμῖν κρίνεται ὁ κόσμος, ἀνάξιοί ἐστε κριτηρίων ἐλαχίστων;
records.gloss: And if by you is judged the world, unworthy are you of cases very small?
pieces: And if the world is to be judged by you, are you not fit to settle the most trivial of cases?

L.2: And if the world is judged by you, are you unworthy of [judging] the smallest cases?

R.2: If you are going to judge the world, surely you can settle small problems like these?

decisions.choice: by you: the holy ones are the ones who judge
decisions.reason: ἐν ὑμῖν with a passive verb most naturally names who does the judging, which follows from verse 2a. Read as "before your court", the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: cases: the disputes being brought to court
alternatives: courts, the places where judgment is given
decisions.reason: κριτηρίων can mean a court (James 2:6) or a case heard in one. With "smallest" the point is the cases themselves: if they will judge the world, these disputes are nothing.

decisions.choice: unworthy: not competent, not fit for a task
decisions.reason: ἀνάξιοί means lacking the standing or the ability for something. The question expects the answer that they are fully able.

decisions.choice: [judging] (L); fit to settle (B); can settle (R)
decisions.reason: English needs a verb to say what they are fit for.

records.source: οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ἀγγέλους κρινοῦμεν, μήτιγε βιωτικά;
records.gloss: Not do you know that angels we will judge, not to speak of things of this life?
pieces: Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more, then, the affairs of everyday life!

L.3: Do you not know that we will judge angels, not to mention matters of this life?

R.3: Do you not know that we will judge angels? Then surely we can judge the ordinary problems of this life!

decisions.choice: angels: most likely the angels who rebelled against God
alternatives: rulers thought to stand behind the nations
decisions.reason: Scripture speaks of angels who sinned and are kept for judgment (2 Peter 2:4; Jude 6). Paul does not say which angels; his point is that God's people will share in judgment on the highest level.

decisions.choice: not to mention: an argument from the greater to the lesser
decisions.reason: μήτιγε means "let alone" or "how much more": if they will judge angels, they can surely deal with everyday disputes.

decisions.choice: matters of this life: ordinary affairs such as money and property
decisions.reason: βιωτικά; describes what belongs to daily living, the business of this present life, as against the age to come.

decisions.choice: a second sentence
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the conclusion as a separate exclamation so that the argument from greater to lesser is clear (m2).

records.source: βιωτικὰ μὲν οὖν κριτήρια ἐὰν ἔχητε, τοὺς ἐξουθενημένους ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ, τούτους καθίζετε;
records.gloss: Matters of this life indeed then if cases you have, those being despised in the church, these do you seat?
pieces: So if you have cases about everyday matters, why do you seat as judges people who count for nothing in the church?

L.4: So if you have cases about matters of this life, do you seat as judges those who are of no account in the church?

R.4: So when you have disputes about everyday things, why do you choose judges who have no standing at all in the church?

decisions.choice: a question: do you really appoint as judges those who have no standing in the church?
alternatives: an ironic command: appoint even the least respected members of the church as judges
decisions.reason: καθίζετε; can be a question or a command. The SBLGNT punctuates it as a question, and this fits verses 1 and 6, where the judges are unbelievers. Read as a command, Paul would be saying sarcastically that the lowliest believer would do better than a pagan court; verse 5, where he looks for someone wise, sits less easily with that.

decisions.choice: of no account in the church: the outside judges, whose verdicts carry no weight in the church's life
alternatives: the lowliest or least respected members of the church
decisions.reason: ἐξουθενημένους means "regarded as nothing". On the reading taken in m1, Paul is not telling believers to despise the judges as people; he means that their judgment has no standing among God's people, who will judge the world.

decisions.choice: cases: disputes needing a decision
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: as judges
decisions.reason: The verb means to seat someone on a judge's bench; English needs the words "as judges" to say so.

records.source: πρὸς ἐντροπὴν ὑμῖν λέγω.
records.gloss: For shame to you I say.
pieces: I say this to shame you.

R.5: I am saying this to make you ashamed.

decisions.choice: to shame you: Paul means them to feel ashamed
decisions.reason: In 4:14 Paul said he did not write to shame them. Here he does: in a culture where honor and shame governed public life, taking a fellow believer before an outside court shamed the church, and Paul wants them to feel it. ἐντροπὴν is the same root as the verb in 4:14.

decisions.choice: this
decisions.reason: English needs an object for "say".

records.source: οὕτως οὐκ ἔνι ἐν ὑμῖν οὐδεὶς σοφὸς ὃς δυνήσεται διακρῖναι ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ, ἀλλὰ ἀδελφὸς μετὰ ἀδελφοῦ κρίνεται, καὶ τοῦτο ἐπὶ ἀπίστων;
records.gloss: So not is there among you no one wise who will be able to decide between the brother of him, \v 6 but brother with brother goes to law, and this before unbelievers?
pieces: Is there really no one among you with wisdom enough to settle a case between {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}},
so that instead believers go to law against one another, and before unbelievers at that?

L.5: Is it so, that there is not among you one wise [person] who will be able to decide between {{gender:his brother or sister|his brother}} [and another],
L.6: but {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} goes to law with {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}, and this before unbelievers?

R.5: Is there not one wise person among you who can settle a quarrel between believers?
R.6: Instead, one believer takes another to court, and lets unbelievers judge the case!

decisions.choice: wise: Paul's irony; a church proud of its wisdom cannot find one wise person
decisions.reason: σοφὸς picks up the theme of 1:18-3:23, where the Corinthians prize wisdom. If they are as wise as they think, someone among them can settle a dispute.

decisions.choice: between his brother: a short way of saying between one believer and another
decisions.reason: The Greek names only one party, "between his brother"; the other party is understood. The sense is a case between two members of the church.

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow member of the church, man or woman
decisions.reason: Paul calls believers brothers as members of one family in Christ. The dispute could be between any two members, so the word includes women.

decisions.choice: unbelievers: the same people called "the unrighteous" in verse 1
decisions.reason: ἀπίστων; makes plain what ἀδίκων meant in verse 1: the judges are people who do not believe. The shame is that the church's quarrels are laid open before them.

decisions.choice: so: introducing an indignant question, "has it come to this?"
decisions.reason: οὕτως here expresses dismay that things are so, rather than pointing back to a particular statement.

decisions.choice: {{gender:his brother or sister|his brother}}, {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} (L); {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} (B)
decisions.reason: The brothers here are any members of the church (m3). Balanced puts the second half as "believers ... against one another" and Readable says "believers", which need no setting.

decisions.choice: believers go to law against one another (B); one believer takes another to court (R)
alternatives: brother goes to law with brother
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say the same thing in natural English, with "believers" for the family word.

records.source: ἤδη μὲν οὖν ὅλως ἥττημα ὑμῖν ἐστιν ὅτι κρίματα ἔχετε μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν· διὰ τί οὐχὶ μᾶλλον ἀδικεῖσθε;
records.gloss: Already indeed then altogether a defeat for you it is that lawsuits you have with yourselves; why not rather are you wronged?
pieces: Simply by having lawsuits against one another you are already defeated, whatever the verdict. Why not accept being wronged instead?

L.7: Already, indeed, it is altogether a defeat for you that you have lawsuits with one another. Why not rather be wronged?

R.7: When you take each other to court, you have already lost, whoever wins the case. Why not simply let yourself be treated unfairly?

decisions.choice: defeat: a loss; they have lost before any case is decided
decisions.reason: ἥττημα means a defeat or loss, and can shade into failure. With ἤδη ("already") and ὅλως ("altogether"), Paul says that going to court against one another is itself a loss, whoever wins.

decisions.choice: let yourselves be wronged: accepting wrong rather than suing
decisions.reason: ἀδικεῖσθε; is a middle or passive form: "allow yourselves to be wronged". Paul asks why they do not choose to suffer the loss.

decisions.choice: perhaps an echo of Jesus' teaching not to resist the one who does wrong
decisions.reason: Jesus taught his followers to give more to the one who sues them rather than fight back (Matthew 5:39-40). Paul does not quote him here, so the echo is possible, not certain.

decisions.choice: with one another: the reflexive used for each other
decisions.reason: ἑαυτῶν (literally "yourselves") is used here, as often, for a relation between members of the group.

decisions.choice: whatever the verdict (B); whoever wins the case (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out what "already" means: the loss comes before any verdict (m1).

records.source: διὰ τί οὐχὶ μᾶλλον ἀποστερεῖσθε;
records.gloss: Why not rather are you defrauded?
pieces: Why not accept being cheated instead?

R.7: Why not simply let yourself be cheated?

decisions.choice: defrauded: robbed of what is rightly one's own
decisions.reason: ἀποστερεῖσθε; means to take or keep back what belongs to another, as in the commandment Jesus quotes in Mark 10:19. It suggests that the lawsuits were about money or property.

decisions.choice: cheated
decisions.reason: "Cheated" is the everyday word; Literal keeps "defrauded".

records.source: ἀλλὰ ὑμεῖς ἀδικεῖτε καὶ ἀποστερεῖτε, καὶ τοῦτο ἀδελφούς.
records.gloss: But you do wrong and defraud, and this brothers.
pieces: Instead, you yourselves do the wronging and the cheating, and to your own {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}!

L.8: But you yourselves do wrong and defraud, and that [to] {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.

R.8: But instead you are the ones who treat others unfairly and cheat them. And you do it to your own {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} in the faith!

decisions.choice: you yourselves: far from accepting wrong, they are the ones who do it
decisions.reason: ὑμεῖς is emphatic. The same two verbs as in verse 7 now have the Corinthians as their subject.

decisions.choice: brothers: fellow believers, men and women, members of one family
decisions.reason: The wrong is worse because it is done within God's family.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: Fellow believers, men and women (m2).

records.source: Ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ἄδικοι θεοῦ βασιλείαν οὐ κληρονομήσουσιν;
records.gloss: Or not do you know that unrighteous [ones] of God [the] kingdom not will inherit?
pieces: Or do you not know that people who do wrong will not receive God's kingdom as their inheritance?

L.9: Or do you not know that [the] unrighteous will not inherit [the] kingdom of God?

R.9: Do you not know that people who do wrong will have no place in God's kingdom?

decisions.choice: the unrighteous: those whose lives are marked by wrongdoing
decisions.reason: ἄδικοι picks up ἀδίκων in verse 1 and the verb in verse 8 ("you do wrong"). The play on words warns the Corinthians: by wronging one another they are acting like the people who will not inherit the kingdom.

decisions.choice: inherit the kingdom of God: receive a share in God's rule when it comes in full
decisions.reason: Israel received the land as an inheritance; in the New Testament God's people inherit his kingdom (15:50; Galatians 5:21; Matthew 25:34). The future tense looks to the end.

decisions.choice: people who do wrong; receive ... as their inheritance (B); have no place in (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the link with verse 8 ("do wrong", m1). Readable says plainly what inheriting the kingdom means.

records.heading: Those who will not inherit the kingdom

records.source: μὴ πλανᾶσθε· οὔτε πόρνοι οὔτε εἰδωλολάτραι οὔτε μοιχοὶ οὔτε μαλακοὶ οὔτε ἀρσενοκοῖται οὔτε κλέπται οὔτε πλεονέκται, οὐ μέθυσοι, οὐ λοίδοροι, οὐχ ἅρπαγες βασιλείαν θεοῦ κληρονομήσουσιν.
records.gloss: Not be deceived: neither sexually immoral nor idolaters nor adulterers nor soft [ones] nor male-bedders \v 10 nor thieves nor greedy [ones], not drunkards, not abusive [ones], not swindlers [the] kingdom of God will inherit.
pieces: Make no mistake: the sexually immoral, idolaters, adulterers, men who take the passive part in sex with men, men who go to bed with males,
thieves, the greedy, drunkards, abusive people, and swindlers: none of these will receive God's kingdom as their inheritance.

L.9: Do not be deceived: neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor soft [men], nor men who lie with males,
L.10: nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor abusive [people], nor swindlers will inherit [the] kingdom of God.

R.9: Do not fool yourselves. People who commit sexual sins, who worship idols, or who are unfaithful in marriage will have no place in God's kingdom. Neither will men who let other men have sex with them, or men who have sex with other men.
R.10: People who steal, who are greedy, who get drunk, who insult people, or who cheat others will have no place in God's kingdom either.

decisions.choice: do not be deceived: stop letting yourselves be led astray
decisions.reason: μὴ πλανᾶσθε warns against a belief that how one lives does not matter for those who belong to God. The sayings Paul quotes in verses 12-13 show such a belief in Corinth.

decisions.choice: the sexually immoral: people who engage in any sexual relationship outside marriage
decisions.reason: πόρνοι is related to the word for a prostitute (verses 15-16) but in lists like this covers every kind of sexual sin, including the case in 5:1. The masculine form is used for everyone, as in such lists generally.

decisions.choice: men who take the passive part in sex between males
alternatives: "soft" in a broad moral sense: men given to luxury and lacking self-control, with no sexual sense in particular
boys or young men kept for sex by older men, or male prostitutes
decisions.reason: μαλακοὶ means "soft": in Matthew 11:8 it describes fine clothing. Said of men, it was a term of contempt for men thought unmanly, and it was used especially of males who let themselves be penetrated by other men, sometimes boys or young men kept for that purpose. Here it stands among sexual sins, between adulterers and ἀρσενοκοῖται, and that setting points to the sexual sense. The word can carry the broader sense of self-indulgence, and some read it that way here. Paul names conduct; he does not describe inclinations or sexual orientation, ideas the Greek words do not contain.

decisions.choice: men who have sex with males
alternatives: men who exploit others sexually, as in the use of boys or of slaves and prostitutes
a broader sense of exploitation, including economic
decisions.reason: ἀρσενοκοῖται joins the words for "male" and "bed" (in the sense of sexual intercourse). It is not found in any surviving Greek writing before Paul; it appears again in 1 Timothy 1:10. The two parts stand side by side in the Greek of Leviticus 20:13, and close together in 18:22, the laws that forbid a man to lie with a male, and the word was most likely formed from those laws. Those laws forbid sex between males of every kind, not only exploitative forms, and with μαλακοὶ beside it the pair most likely names both partners. Some argue that the word, being new and rare, meant something narrower, such as sexual exploitation of others. Again Paul names acts, not orientation.

decisions.choice: abusive people: those who insult and revile others; swindlers: those who seize what is not theirs, by force or by fraud
alternatives: slanderers; robbers in the narrow sense
decisions.reason: λοίδοροι are people who hurl abuse at others with their words. ἅρπαγες are grasping people who take others' goods by force or by fraud; the word looks back to the defrauding in verses 7-8. Both appear in the list of 5:11.

decisions.choice: the greedy: people always grasping for more, at the expense of others
decisions.reason: πλεονέκται describes those who want more than their share; Colossians 3:5 calls such greed idolatry.

decisions.choice: the list describes ways of life persisted in, not sins beyond forgiveness
decisions.reason: Paul warns that those who live like this will not inherit the kingdom, but verse 11 says at once that some of the Corinthians once lived like this and have been washed, made holy and put right with God. The list includes greed and abusive speech alongside sexual sins; no one item stands apart from the others.

decisions.choice: soft [men], men who lie with males (L); men who take the passive part in sex with men, men who go to bed with males (B); men who let other men have sex with them, men who have sex with other men (R)
decisions.reason: The two Greek words stay two items at every level (m3, m4). "Homosexuals" names an orientation, a modern idea the Greek words do not express; "effeminate" in modern English describes manner, not conduct; "sodomites" brings in a later reading of Genesis 19. Literal keeps "soft" so the reader can see the Greek word, and "lie with males" keeps the echo of Leviticus.

decisions.choice: the list first, then "none of these will receive God's kingdom" (B); two sentences, each ending "will have no place in God's kingdom" (R)
decisions.reason: A long chain of "neither ... nor" is hard to follow aloud. Balanced lists the people first and then sums up; Readable breaks the list into short sentences.

decisions.choice: abusive [people], swindlers (L); abusive people, swindlers (B); insult people, cheat others (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:10-11, where the same words appear: "revilers" is little used today, and "swindlers" covers taking by fraud as well as by force (m5).

records.source: καὶ ταῦτά τινες ἦτε· ἀλλὰ ἀπελούσασθε, ἀλλὰ ἡγιάσθητε, ἀλλὰ ἐδικαιώθητε ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ καὶ ἐν τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν.
records.gloss: And these things some [of you] were; but you were washed, but you were made holy, but you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus and in the Spirit of the God of us.
pieces: Some of you once lived in these ways. But you have been washed clean; you have been made holy; you have been put right with God, in the name of the Lord Jesus and through the Spirit of our God.

L.11: And such were some [of you]. But you were washed, but you were made holy, but you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of our God.

R.11: Some of you used to be like that. But God has washed your sins away. He has made you holy and has put you right with {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}. All this happened through the name of the Lord Jesus and through the Spirit of our God.

decisions.choice: such were some of you: a past way of life, now left behind
decisions.reason: The neuter ταῦτά ("these things") sums up the list: this is what some of them were. The past tense ἦτε marks it as over.

decisions.choice: washed: cleansed from sin, probably with baptism in view
alternatives: a cleansing with no reference to baptism
decisions.reason: ἀπελούσασθε can mean "you had yourselves washed", and Acts 22:16 joins being baptized and washing away sins. Paul's point is the cleansing itself, which God gives.

decisions.choice: three ways of describing one change God has made, not three stages in order
alternatives: three steps, one after the other
decisions.reason: Each verb is introduced by ἀλλὰ ("but") and all are in the same past tense. Being washed, made holy and put right with God describe from three sides what happened when they came to Christ, and the sentence names the Lord Jesus, the Spirit and God together as its source.

decisions.choice: justified: declared righteous by God, acquitted at his court
decisions.reason: ἐδικαιώθητε is a word of the law court. In a chapter about believers taking one another to court, Paul reminds them of the verdict God has already given in their favor (compare Romans 5:1; 8:33).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the Lord Jesus"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "Christ", and some "our"; the SBLGNT has the shorter text. The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the manuscript evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: put right with God (B); put you right with himself (R)
decisions.reason: "Justified" is a church word to many readers; "put right with God" says what God's verdict does (m4). Literal keeps "justified".

decisions.choice: God has washed your sins away. He has made you holy ...
alternatives: you were washed, made holy, justified
decisions.reason: The passive verbs mean that God did these things; Readable names him and says what was washed away (m2).

records.source: Πάντα μοι ἔξεστιν· ἀλλ’ οὐ πάντα συμφέρει.
records.gloss: All things to me are lawful; but not all things are beneficial.
pieces: "Everything is permitted for me." Yes, but not everything is for the good.

L.12: "All things are permitted to me"; but not all things are of benefit.

R.12: Some of you say, "I am allowed to do anything." That may be true, but not everything is good for you.

decisions.choice: the words are a saying used in Corinth, which Paul quotes and then qualifies; they are marked as a quotation
alternatives: Paul's own principle, which he then limits
decisions.reason: The Greek has no quotation marks, so this is a judgment. The same saying comes back in this verse and again twice in 10:23, each time followed by Paul's "but". Without limits, "all things are permitted" would contradict what Paul has just said in verses 9-10. It may be the Corinthians' own use of Paul's teaching on freedom, now turned to excuse sexual sin.

decisions.choice: permitted: there is no rule against it; one has the right to do it
alternatives: legal under the law of the land
decisions.reason: ἔξεστιν means "it is allowed". The saying claims a believer's freedom to do as one likes, here with the body.

decisions.choice: beneficial: doing real good, to oneself and to others
decisions.reason: συμφέρει means to help or profit. In 10:23-24 and 12:7 Paul measures it by the good of others as well.

decisions.choice: permitted (L, B); allowed (R)
decisions.reason: "Lawful" now suggests the law of the land; the saying is about freedom from rules.

decisions.choice: Yes, but (B); Some of you say ... That may be true, but (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that Paul grants the saying in part before he limits it (m1); Readable says whose saying it is.

records.heading: Your body belongs to the Lord

records.source: πάντα μοι ἔξεστιν· ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐγὼ ἐξουσιασθήσομαι ὑπό τινος.
records.gloss: All things to me are lawful; but not I will be brought under authority by anything.
pieces: "Everything is permitted for me." Yes, but I will not let anything become my master.

L.12: "All things are permitted to me"; but I will not be brought under the power of anything.

R.12: "I am allowed to do anything." Yes, but I will not let anything control me.

decisions.choice: the Corinthian saying again, marked as a quotation
decisions.reason: As in the first half of the verse (12.s1, m1).

decisions.choice: a play on words: I have the right to all things, but nothing will have the right over me
decisions.reason: ἔξεστιν ("it is permitted") and ἐξουσιασθήσομαι ("I will be brought under the power") come from related words. Paul turns the saying round: freedom used for one's appetites becomes slavery to them.

decisions.choice: anything
alternatives: anyone, perhaps pointing ahead to the prostitute in verse 15
decisions.reason: τινος can be neuter or masculine. The neuter fits the general saying and the appetites of verse 13.

decisions.choice: let anything become my master (B); let anything control me (R)
decisions.reason: An active wording makes Paul's resolve plain and keeps the picture of a master (m2).

records.source: τὰ βρώματα τῇ κοιλίᾳ, καὶ ἡ κοιλία τοῖς βρώμασιν· ὁ δὲ θεὸς καὶ ταύτην καὶ ταῦτα καταργήσει.
records.gloss: The foods for the stomach, and the stomach for the foods; but God both this and these will do away with.
pieces: "Food exists for the stomach and the stomach for food, and in the end God will do away with them both."

L.13: "Foods [are] for the stomach and the stomach for foods, and God will do away with both it and them."

R.13: You also say, "Food is for the stomach, and the stomach is for food. And someday God will put an end to both of them."

decisions.choice: the whole sentence is a second Corinthian saying, marked as a quotation
alternatives: only the first half is the saying, and "God will do away with both" is Paul's own comment
decisions.reason: Paul's reply in verses 13b-14 matches the sentence part for part: the body is not for sexual immorality but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body; God raised the Lord and will raise us. That reply answers "God will do away with both", which suggests these words belong to the saying. Read as Paul's comment, they would say only that food and stomach are temporary.

decisions.choice: the saying's reasoning: bodily appetites are natural and passing, so what one does with the body does not matter
decisions.reason: The saying treats the body as a set of appetites that will perish. The next sentence shows that some applied the same reasoning to sex, which is why Paul answers with the body and sexual immorality.

decisions.choice: stomach: the belly, the organ of eating
decisions.reason: κοιλίᾳ is the belly or stomach, and could stand for bodily appetite (Philippians 3:19).

decisions.choice: do away with: bring to an end, make of no effect
decisions.reason: καταργήσει means to put out of action or bring to nothing, as in 1:28 and 2:6.

decisions.choice: You also say
decisions.reason: Readable says that this is the Corinthians' saying (m1).

records.source: τὸ δὲ σῶμα οὐ τῇ πορνείᾳ ἀλλὰ τῷ κυρίῳ, καὶ ὁ κύριος τῷ σώματι·
records.gloss: But the body not for the sexual immorality but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body;
pieces: The body, however, does not exist for sexual immorality; it exists for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.

L.13: But the body [is] not for sexual immorality but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.

R.13: But the body is not for sexual sin. It is for the Lord, and the Lord cares about the body.

decisions.choice: the body is not like the stomach: it is the whole person in bodily life, and it belongs to the Lord
decisions.reason: Paul answers the saying in its own form. σῶμα is not one organ among others but the self as it lives and acts in the world, and it belongs to the Lord who will raise it (verse 14).

decisions.choice: sexual immorality: any sexual relationship outside marriage, here above all with prostitutes
decisions.reason: πορνείᾳ covers every kind of sexual sin (5:1); verses 15-16 show that sex with prostitutes is in view.

decisions.choice: the Lord for the body: the Lord is committed to the body and has a purpose for it
decisions.reason: The Lord does not treat the body as worthless; he claims it and will raise it from death (verse 14; 15:42-44).

decisions.choice: does not exist for ... it exists for
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the same verb as in the saying ("Food exists for the stomach") so the reader hears Paul answering it.

decisions.choice: the Lord cares about the body
decisions.reason: Readable gives a verb for the short Greek phrase (m3).

records.source: ὁ δὲ θεὸς καὶ τὸν κύριον ἤγειρεν καὶ ἡμᾶς ἐξεγερεῖ διὰ τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: But God both the Lord raised and us will raise up through the power of him.
pieces: God raised the Lord, and by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will raise us as well.

L.14: And God both raised the Lord and will raise us up through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power.

R.14: God raised the Lord Jesus from death, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will use {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power to raise us too.

decisions.choice: Paul's answer to "God will do away with both": God will not do away with the body but raise it
decisions.reason: ὁ δὲ θεὸς matches the end of the saying in verse 13. What God does with the body is resurrection, not destruction, so the body matters now.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "will raise"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have the present or the past tense instead of the future. The future fits the contrast with Christ's resurrection, already past. Reviewers should check the manuscript evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: his power: God's power
decisions.reason: αὐτοῦ refers back to God, the subject of the sentence.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus from death
decisions.reason: Readable names the Lord and says what he was raised from.

records.source: οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι τὰ σώματα ὑμῶν μέλη Χριστοῦ ἐστιν;
records.gloss: Not do you know that the bodies of you members of Christ are?
pieces: Do you not know that your bodies are parts of {{christos:Christ's|the Messiah's}} body?

L.15: Do you not know that your bodies are members of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?

R.15: Do you not know that your bodies belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} as parts of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own body?

decisions.choice: members: limbs and organs, the parts of a body
decisions.reason: μέλη are the parts of a body, as in 12:12-27. The believer's body is joined to Christ as a hand or foot is joined to a body.

decisions.choice: the believer's own physical body is joined to Christ
alternatives: only the church as a whole is Christ's body
decisions.reason: Here Paul speaks of their bodies, plural: what each person does with the body is done with something that belongs to Christ.

decisions.choice: parts of Christ's body (B); belong to Christ as parts of his own body (R)
decisions.reason: "Members" now usually means members of a club; Balanced and Readable keep the picture of a body (m1).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ's|the Messiah's}} (B); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

records.source: ἄρας οὖν τὰ μέλη τοῦ Χριστοῦ ποιήσω πόρνης μέλη;
records.gloss: Taking away then the members of the Christ shall I make of a prostitute members?
pieces: Am I then to take parts of {{christos:Christ's|the Messiah's}} body and make them parts of a prostitute's body?

L.15: Taking, then, the members of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, shall I make [them] members of a prostitute?

R.15: So should I take parts of {{christos:Christ's|the Messiah's}} body and join them to a prostitute?

decisions.choice: I: Paul uses himself as the example
decisions.reason: ποιήσω is first person. Paul puts the question to himself to show how unthinkable it is for any believer.

decisions.choice: taking away: removing the members from Christ
decisions.reason: ἄρας can mean to take up or to take away. Joining one's body to a prostitute is pictured as taking it away from Christ.

decisions.choice: a prostitute: a woman who sold sex, a common part of life in Greek and Roman cities
decisions.reason: Prostitution was legal and widespread, and many men saw visits to prostitutes, often after banquets, as normal. Some of the Corinthian believers seem to have kept to this custom.

decisions.choice: parts of Christ's body (B, R); parts of a prostitute's body (B); join them to a prostitute (R)
decisions.reason: As in 15.s1.

records.source: μὴ γένοιτο.
records.gloss: Not may it be.
pieces: Absolutely not!

decisions.choice: the strongest possible rejection
decisions.reason: μὴ γένοιτο is Paul's way of rejecting a thought with horror (Romans 6:2, 15; Galatians 2:17).

decisions.choice: Absolutely not (B); No, never (R)
decisions.reason: "God forbid" adds God's name, which the Greek does not have.

records.source: ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ὁ κολλώμενος τῇ πόρνῃ ἓν σῶμά ἐστιν;
records.gloss: Or not do you know that the [one] joining himself to the prostitute one body is?
pieces: Or do you not know that a man who attaches himself to a prostitute forms one body with her?

L.16: Or do you not know that the one who joins himself to the prostitute is one body [with her]?

R.16: Do you not know that a man who has sex with a prostitute becomes one body with her?

decisions.choice: joins himself: is closely united, here in sexual union
decisions.reason: κολλώμενος means to stick to or cling to. The Greek of Genesis 2:24 uses the same verb for a man clinging to his wife, and verse 17 uses it of being joined to the Lord.

decisions.choice: the man who visits a prostitute
decisions.reason: The participle is masculine, and in this setting it means men who went to prostitutes (m3 in 15.s2).

decisions.choice: one body: sexual union makes a real bond between two people, not a passing act
decisions.reason: Paul takes sex to unite two persons, as Genesis says of marriage. What the body does involves the whole person.

decisions.choice: [with her] (L); with her (B, R)
decisions.reason: English needs to say with whom he is one body.

records.source: Ἔσονται γάρ, φησίν, οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν.
records.gloss: Will be for, he says, the two into flesh one.
pieces: For Scripture says, "The two will be united into one flesh."

L.16: For, it says, "The two will be one flesh."

R.16: As Scripture says, "The two will become one body."

decisions.choice: a quotation of Genesis 2:24
decisions.reason: The words are from Genesis 2:24, where a man leaves his parents and clings to his wife. The Greek Old Testament has "the two", which the Hebrew text does not have; Jesus quotes the verse in the same form (Matthew 19:5; Mark 10:8). Reviewers should check the wording against the Greek Old Testament.

decisions.choice: it says: Scripture says
decisions.reason: φησίν has no stated subject. It can mean "it says", the usual way of introducing Scripture, or "he says", meaning God, as Jesus treats this verse as the Creator's word (Matthew 19:4-5). Either way the words carry God's authority.

decisions.choice: become one flesh: become a single unit of life, as in marriage
decisions.reason: εἰς σάρκα μίαν follows a Hebrew way of saying "become one flesh". In Genesis it describes the union of husband and wife. Paul applies it to the union with a prostitute: even that act makes a bond of the kind God made for marriage.

decisions.choice: Scripture says
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "it" is (m2).

decisions.choice: one flesh (L, B); one body (R)
decisions.reason: In this quotation "flesh" means a human being in bodily life, not "merely human", so Literal and Balanced keep the familiar words of Genesis. Readable says "one body", which links the verse with the first half of verse 16.

decisions.choice: united into
decisions.reason: The Greek "will be into" means "will become"; Balanced gives it a full English verb.

records.source: ὁ δὲ κολλώμενος τῷ κυρίῳ ἓν πνεῦμά ἐστιν.
records.gloss: But the [one] joining himself to the Lord one spirit is.
pieces: But anyone who is joined to the Lord is one spirit with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.17: But the one who is joined to the Lord is one spirit [with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}].

R.17: But anyone who is joined to the Lord is one with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in spirit.

decisions.choice: the same verb as in verse 16, set in contrast; here it means any believer
decisions.reason: κολλώμενος repeats the word used of the man and the prostitute. The masculine form here is general: anyone, man or woman, who belongs to the Lord.

decisions.choice: one spirit: united with the Lord through the Holy Spirit
alternatives: united only in the human spirit, apart from the body
decisions.reason: Union with the Lord is made by the Spirit (12:13), and verse 19 says the Spirit lives in the believer's body. This is not a spiritual union that leaves the body out: verse 15 has already said the body is joined to Christ.

decisions.choice: the believer's union with the Lord rules out union with a prostitute
decisions.reason: The two unions cannot be held together: the one joined to the Lord cannot also join the Lord's members to a prostitute (verse 15).

decisions.choice: [with him] (L); with him (B, R)
decisions.reason: English needs to say with whom the believer is one.

records.source: φεύγετε τὴν πορνείαν· πᾶν ἁμάρτημα ὃ ἐὰν ποιήσῃ ἄνθρωπος ἐκτὸς τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν, ὁ δὲ πορνεύων εἰς τὸ ἴδιον σῶμα ἁμαρτάνει.
records.gloss: Flee the sexual immorality; every sin which if does a person outside the body is, but the [one] committing sexual immorality into the own body sins.
pieces: Get away from sexual immorality! Whatever other sin someone commits stays outside the body, but the one who is sexually immoral sins against {{gender:their|his}} very own body.

L.18: Flee sexual immorality. Every sin that a {{gender:person|man}} commits is outside the body, but the one who commits sexual immorality sins against [{{gender:their|his}}] own body.

R.18: Run away from sexual sin! No other sin touches the body the way it does. People who commit sexual sin are sinning against their own bodies.

decisions.choice: flee: keep running from it, a continuing command
decisions.reason: φεύγετε is a present imperative: make a habit of getting away. Joseph's flight from Potiphar's wife (Genesis 39:12) is the classic picture of such a flight.

decisions.choice: Paul's own words: no other sin involves the body as sexual sin does
alternatives: another Corinthian saying, "every sin a person commits is outside the body", which Paul answers with "but"
decisions.reason: The Greek has no quotation marks. Some read the middle clause as a saying like those in verses 12-13, claiming that what the body does cannot touch the self, and Paul's reply as following it. Read as Paul's own words, the clause is a comparison rather than an absolute: other sins harm the body too, but sexual sin is done with the body against the body, joining it to another.

decisions.choice: against one's own body: a sin against the body that belongs to the Lord
decisions.reason: εἰς here means "against". The body is joined to the Lord (verse 15) and is the Spirit's temple (verse 19), so sexual sin wrongs one's own body in a unique way.

decisions.choice: a person: anyone, man or woman
decisions.reason: ἄνθρωπος is general.

decisions.choice: other (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "other" to show that sexual sin is being set apart from every other sin (m2). Readable states the comparison plainly.

decisions.choice: {{gender:person|man}} (L); {{gender:their|his}} (L, B)
decisions.reason: The person meant is anyone, man or woman (m4). Readable uses the plural, which needs no setting.

records.source: ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι τὸ σῶμα ὑμῶν ναὸς τοῦ ἐν ὑμῖν ἁγίου πνεύματός ἐστιν, οὗ ἔχετε ἀπὸ θεοῦ;
records.gloss: Or not do you know that the body of you temple of the in you Holy Spirit is, whom you have from God?
pieces: Or do you not know that your body is a temple where the Holy Spirit lives, the Spirit who is in you and whom God has given you?

L.19: Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit [who is] in you, [the Spirit] whom you have from God?

R.19: Do you not know that your body is a temple, a home for the Holy Spirit? The Spirit lives in you, and God is the one who gave you the Spirit.

decisions.choice: temple: the sanctuary itself, the house where God lives
decisions.reason: As in 3:16, ναὸς is the inner house of a temple, where the deity was thought to be present.

decisions.choice: each believer's body is a temple of the Spirit
alternatives: the church as a whole is the body that is the temple, as in 3:16
decisions.reason: "Your" is plural but σῶμα is singular. In 3:16 the church is God's temple; here, after verses 15-18 on what each person does with the body, Paul applies the picture to each believer's body, while still addressing them all together.

decisions.choice: whom you have from God: the Spirit is God's gift
decisions.reason: The relative οὗ refers to the Spirit. The Spirit is not something they own by nature; God has given the Spirit to them, so the body that houses the Spirit is not theirs to use as they like (verse 19b).

decisions.choice: a temple where the Holy Spirit lives (B); a home for the Holy Spirit (R)
alternatives: a temple of the Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what makes the body a temple: the Spirit lives in it.

records.source: καὶ οὐκ ἐστὲ ἑαυτῶν, ἠγοράσθητε γὰρ τιμῆς· δοξάσατε δὴ τὸν θεὸν ἐν τῷ σώματι ὑμῶν.
records.gloss: And not you are of yourselves, \v 20 you were bought for at a price; glorify then the God in the body of you.
pieces: You do not belong to yourselves.
You were bought, and a price was paid for you. So bring glory to God in your body.

L.19: And you do not belong to yourselves;
L.20: for you were bought for a price. Glorify God, then, in your body.

R.19: You do not belong to yourselves anymore.
R.20: God bought you and paid the price for you. So use your body to bring glory to God.

decisions.choice: bought: as a slave is bought, so that the believer now belongs to a new master
alternatives: set free by a purchase, as when a slave was freed
decisions.reason: ἠγοράσθητε is the ordinary word for buying, and buying people meant the slave market. In 7:22-23 Paul uses the same picture: "you were bought at a price; do not become slaves of people." The point here is ownership: they belong to God.

decisions.choice: a price: a real cost was paid, the death of Christ
decisions.reason: τιμῆς is a genitive of price: "at a price". Paul does not name the price here, but elsewhere he speaks of Christ's death as the cost of redemption (Galatians 3:13; compare 1 Peter 1:18-19).

decisions.choice: glorify: honor God and show his worth by what one does
decisions.reason: δοξάσατε is a command: with the body that belongs to God, do what brings him honor. The body itself is the place where God is honored, not something to be set aside.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: the sentence ends with "in your body"
alternatives: many later manuscripts add "and in your spirit, which are God's"
decisions.reason: The longer ending is found in many later manuscripts and in the King James Version, but not in the oldest manuscripts, which the SBLGNT follows. Reviewers should check the manuscript evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: for ... then: the purchase is the reason they are not their own, and the command follows from it
decisions.reason: γὰρ gives the reason for verse 19b, and δὴ draws the conclusion with force.

decisions.choice: glorify (L); bring glory to (B, R)
decisions.reason: Key term: the verb stays with the word "glory" at every level.

decisions.choice: a price was paid for you (B); God bought you and paid the price for you (R)
alternatives: you were bought at a price
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the genitive of price a clause; Readable names God as the buyer, which the passive implies (m1, m2), and adds "anymore" in verse 19 to show the change of owner.
